text:
Maria: quick sync — I'm sketching the UX for a 'mismatch tolerance' knob in automatic fallback policies. Goal: make rollouts safe when model output shape drifts but still allow graceful degradation. thoughts?
Ken: agree we need something more expressive than a single on/off. maybe levels: strict | tolerant | preview-sample?
Samir: +1. also need to capture WHY it fell back. Operators should see the trigger: schema-violation, latency spike, or error-classifier score.
Jess: can we show a short forensic card in the UI: trigger, sample input, model output, fallback output, decision-id, and a link to the audit trace?
Maria: yes — prototype idea: when a request triggers fallback, UI surfaces a compact banner: "Fallback engaged — schema mismatch (field: address.line1)". click expands to forensic card.
Ken: important: sampling rates. we should let teams sample 0.1% / 1% / 10% of fallbacks to keep production traffic routed to original model for debugging. :mag:
Samir: telemetry note — every fallback needs a deterministic decision-id so we can correlate logs, traces, eval snapshots. also store a compact delta of model vs fallback output for quick diffs.
Jess: UX affordance: toggle between "explain" and "silent" modes. explain shows the card inline to engineers, silent only logs and notifies on thresholds.
Maria: policy control proposal (in UI and config):
```
policy.mismatch_tolerance:
  mode: tolerant  # strict | tolerant | preview
  triggers:
    - schema_violation: {threshold: 1} # immediate
    - error_classifier: {score_gt: 0.8}
  sampling: 0.01 # fraction of fallbacks that still route to primary for traces
  audit_retention_days: 30
```
Ken: love the config snippet. question: what about cascading fallbacks? e.g. primary->light-degrade->hard-fallback. UI should let you preview the handoff chain.
Maria: yep. show each hop with estimated latency delta and cost delta. and allow quick rewind to previous hop.
Samir: for autoscaling and SLA implications, add a small inline estimator: "expected tail latency + p50/p95 if enabled" before saving policy.
Jess: ops story: we need an operator override in console: "force-primary for X minutes" with audit reason required. also record operator id + ticket link.
Maria: agree — require reason. show agent badge in audit trace.
ops-bot: @channel canary deployed mismatch-tolerance v0.3 to rtx-canary at 1789994550 — 50 requests sampled.
deploy-bot: canary result: 50 sampled, 3 fallbacks, error-classifier avg 0.72. full results at https://console.redwood.internal/canaries/1789994550
Ken: next design task: mockups for forensic card + policy editor flow. I'll take the mockups.
Samir: I'll write the telemetry schema and ensure decision_id + compact diff are in logs.
Jess: I'll draft the operator-runbook (how to triage mismatches) and the UI copy for the banner.
Maria: sweet. action items: @Ken mockups, @Samir telemetry schema PR, @Jess runbook draft. let's sync Wed 10am. :calendar: 
Ken: noted. ping if you want a walkthrough beforehand.
Maria: thanks all — want this to be very lightweight in the console so teams actually use it, but auditable enough for enterprise customers.
